question: Can movement and sprint timing beat plain W-tap in MMC boxing when both fighters keep clicking at the same rate?
settings: Provisional MMC sprint-at-attack-entry, full 3-block reach, flat boxing court, ordinary mouse tracking, zero extra reaction delay. Fixed 10 CPS on both sides. Test both seats at 0/0 and 80/80 ms RTT. The bot uses only its own client observations.
archive_scan: Report an uninterrupted run once when it reaches its second fresh hit within 850 ms. Any accepted opposing hit ends the run, including a damage upgrade or an opposing hit on the second hit's server tick. Also report doubles after an isolated pair of opposing fresh hits within 75 ms. Compare 750 and 1000 ms activity cutoffs. Keep 10 CPS historical combat profiles and 20 CPS opening-drill results separate. Never count the 20 CPS free opening.
search: Use the original sixteen training calendars in protocol.json and keep the eight development-selection calendars separate. Change only the two scores that control forward/backward movement and Ctrl. Pin clicking open and leave strafe and jump off. Evaluate against plain W-tap on identical clocks in paired 24-second bouts from neutral. Train linear and feedforward variants for 24 generations each. Optimize improvement over the same-seat W-tap mirror in accepted hit margin, fresh hit margin and doubles for minus doubles against. Retain the weaker RTT stratum in the objective.
selection: Screen each retained checkpoint from both seats on all eight exposed development clocks. Require a positive mean accepted margin improvement at both RTTs, positive aggregate net doubles improvement and at least as many activity-qualified cycles over the matched three-hit starts. Rank eligible checkpoints by fewest paired K3 losses, first-to-100 wins, poorer RTT's median paired accepted margin, and net doubles. Freeze the selected weights before any prospective calendar is collected.
native: Test the frozen regulation bot from the beginning against plain W-tap with both clicking immediately. Test a separate copy that plays W-tap to the native three-hit landmark, against the same active W-tap defender after the two-second acquisition protocol. Run two independent repeats per side and RTT for both candidate and control. Report observed click delivery, score, fresh hits, both sides' doubles, and K3, K5 and K10 survival with and without the 1000 ms activity cutoff. Native repeats use independent clocks. Export stages only from the regulation W-tap mirrors to form the prospective model panel. Never train or select on those tapes.
